title: Comparing Nile vessels side by side
standfirst: The same route, three very different trips. Compare dahabiyas, cruise ships and paddle steamers on what matters: how many guests, where you moor, how free the days are and what you pay for. This page is part of our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: The differences that matter
paragraphs: Size decides most things. A dahabiya with a dozen guests and a ship with a hundred and forty sail past the same temples, but the days feel completely different: how long you wait at the gangway, how quiet the evenings are and how much the programme can change.
Moorings matter too. Ships tie up at town quays, often side by side; dahabiyas moor at riverbanks and islands. The comparison below sets these out with figures from our vessel directory.

sections.heading: Price
paragraphs: Prices overlap more than you might expect. The vessel type sets the range, but the cabin, the crew per guest and the season decide where in that range a cruise sits.

faqs.q: Which is better, a dahabiya or a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Neither is better in general. A dahabiya suits travellers who want a small group and quiet; a ship suits those who want facilities and a set programme.

faqs.q: Do all vessels visit the same sites?
faqs.a: The main temples are on every itinerary. Dahabiyas can add smaller sites because they moor away from the towns.
